mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts (HOUST) above 1400K units, indicating strong demand, boosts consumer confidence, leading to increased spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 50% of instances when HOUST > 1400K, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 4% signals accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as investors seek higher yields in equities.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns when FEDFUNDS < 4% are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) drops below 4%, indicating a tight labor market, and payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows by more than 200K in a month, the combined effect predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as a strong labor market fuels economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of instances when both conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a quarter, signaling reduced supply chain pressures, leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as decreased production costs boost corporate profitability.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns after significant INDPRO declines are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Real disposable personal income (RSAFS) growth exceeding 5% in a month, indicating strong consumer demand, predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as increased spending boosts economic activity.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 50% of instances when RSAFS growth > 5%, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 5.5%, signaling tightening monetary policy, predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as higher borrowing costs reduce economic activity.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 5% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth is negative for two consecutive months, the combined effect predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as a weakening labor market signals economic slowdown.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5% and PAYEMS growth < 0 for 2 months
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 40% of instances when both conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: GDP (GDPC1) growth exceeding 3.5% in a quarter, indicating robust economic activity, predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as strong growth boosts corporate earnings and investor sentiment.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns when GDPC1 growth > 3.5% are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
